criterion_scores.reasoning: I checked the document for internally followable rules across its major workflow sections. The main defect is the contradiction between the supposedly universal 'three floors' at lines 45-47 and the existence of pre-event / roundup formats at lines 74-76 and 92-94, which cannot satisfy a physically-attended 'receipts' requirement. There is also a smaller rule conflict between 'No CTA' for post-event recaps (line 76) and the mandated CTA on a carousel final slide (line 250). The rest of the guidance is largely coherent, but these are real operational contradictions.

The artifact covers voice, audience, structure, budgets, DMs, visuals, and workflow in substantial depth. However, it leaves an allowed case under-specified: lines 183-186 allow intentionally text-only posts, while lines 190-193 prescribe '3 Briefs' per post without saying what to do when no visual is desired. The doc is therefore broadly complete but not fully complete on its own stated exception paths.

What I could verify from the artifact itself aligns with the supplied house context: `.claude/references/...` and `.claude/skills/...` paths are used in the expected style, and there is no visible forbidden `alex:` project-skill naming, MCP misuse, or tombstoned tooling in the supplied checks. I cannot earn a 1.0 here because broader repo-wide convention conformance and referenced non-`.claude` materials were not independently inspectable from this artifact alone.

The document is practical rather than over-engineered, but it repeatedly leans on precise, unsourced numerics as if they were stable operating truths: the screen-space percentages at lines 197-199 and the engagement multiplier at lines 245-246. The rubric explicitly calls out fabricated numbers/specificity as an anti-pattern, so this criterion is meaningfully dragged down despite the guide otherwise being lean and action-oriented.

The document is well organized and legible, with clear sectioning and actionable rules. But diagnostics in this rubric also include honesty about what's actually verified. Line 98 explicitly labels a platform limit as 'verified June 2026' with no citation or evidence trail, which is a direct confidence-framing defect. Because that claim is load-bearing for downstream outputs, I searched for and found a real diagnostics issue rather than just a cosmetic nit.

defects.location: lines 45-47, Audience-First North-Star / The three floors
defects.description: This declares a universal requirement set for 'every post', but floor 1 immediately requires a detail only possible from physically attending the event. That is impossible for the pre-event and roundup formats defined later (lines 74-76, 92-94), so the rule set is internally inconsistent on a load-bearing workflow.

defects.location: lines 183-193, Visual Content / Visual Output Per Post
defects.description: The doc says not all posts need a visual (lines 183-186), but this mandatory-sounding section does not state the carve-out or expected output when a text-only post is intentionally chosen. The production guidance is therefore incomplete for that allowed case.

defects.quote: - **Final slide (CTA):** "Follow for more" or a specific question that drives comments.
defects.description: This conflicts with the earlier content-type rule that post-event recaps have 'No CTA' (line 76). The artifact needs to distinguish caption CTAs from carousel-slide CTAs or scope the rule by content type.

defects.quote: **The LinkedIn feed-post hard cap is 3,000 characters** (stable since June 2023; verified June 2026).
defects.description: This presents an external platform constraint as 'verified' without any citation or evidence trail. Because the rule is operationally load-bearing and explicitly framed as verified, this is a confidence/honesty defect under the rubric.

defects.quote: Carousels (uploaded as LinkedIn PDFs) get ~1.5-2x the engagement of single images
defects.description: This is unsourced performance specificity used as policy guidance. In a house style guide, that reads as anecdotal or fabricated precision rather than durable convention.

defects.quote: ~20% more vertical screen space than 1:1 and ~65% more than 16:9, which directly
defects.description: The exact comparative percentages and causal claim about dwell-time impact are presented without support. That is the rubric's fabricated-specificity anti-pattern: precise numbers that look authoritative but are not grounded here.
